The first DataTable body row has a top divider, including when callers visually hide column headings.

Classes on native-attribute components accept Svelte class arrays and objects. Where a structural component exposes `class`, it adds a root hook. No class replacement API is supported. Use finite variants for existing appearances; caller-authored snippet classes own feature text and arrangements. The recipes show those classes explicitly.

Tokens in [tokens.css](tokens.css) own colors, spacing, type and focus. Override `--accent` on a container for another palette, such as `var(--accent-funder)`. The Exposed wordmark stays white across entity contexts. The landing heading uses member purple for MPs and funder teal for financial interests. Entity indicators, badges, highlights, charts and declared values derive their colors from the local accent; a ResultRow root `class` can select that palette explicitly. Actions use neutral `--action`, `--action-ink`, `--action-border`, `--action-surface` and `--action-hover`; all focus rings use `--focus-color`, independently of entity palettes. Keep action and focus tokens neutral in member and funder containers. `--focus-width` and `--focus-offset` apply at the root or on a container. Native links, buttons and summaries add one pixel to the offset. Do not import internal stylesheets individually.

The [barrel](index.ts) is the public inventory. The gallery covers native disclosure/input behavior, precise metric overflow, repeated association IDs and pointer tooltip lifecycle. Financial parsing and availability decisions belong in feature adapters, never in UI components.

UI-owned snippet classes are `.results-list` (list reset and divider), `.entity-text` (shrinkable content), `.entity-name` (result anchor typography and hover), `.entity-alias` (secondary result text), `.funding-list` (nested list reset and spacing), `.declaration-reference`, `.payment-type`, `.currency-label`, `.empty-entry` (declaration context), `.amount` (exact value typography), and `.entry-count`/`.partial-note` (secondary chart/table text). These work with the single UI stylesheet import. Feature grids and custom table columns stay in callers.

`CategoryWheel` accepts `CategoryWheelOption[]` with caller-owned closed SVG sector `path`, open outer-boundary `rimPath` in the same local coordinates, and label positions, a selected identity, accessible group `label`, optional pixel `size` (default 284), and `onselect`. Native pressed buttons cover the complete sectors. Muted category surfaces, icons, labels and fine inner/radial boundaries stay constant. Selection brightens only the outer rim; focus uses a neutral full-sector outline. A decorative neutral chart glyph occupies the center. Each option has optional `width` and `height`, both defaulting to 142px, for its native button bounds. Callers provide `left` and `top` within the 284px canvas and paths and label positions local to those bounds. Sectors must provide their full bounds so the native hit target covers the path. The gallery updates example uses 284px-wide horizontal halves; ranking quadrants use the default square bounds. Features provide a size that fits the layout.

`RankingList` accepts formatted `RankingRow[]` and an accessible list `label`. Features supply stable keys, destinations, amounts, coverage, signs and bar widths. The list animates row and bar entry and disables animation for reduced motion. Party identities can omit destinations.

`ContentChange` takes a string `changeKey` and `children` snippet. Its persistent root fades new committed content from opacity 0.65 to 1 over 200ms. Initial rendering is static. New changes cancel earlier motion; reduced motion skips animation and cancels active motion when enabled. Keep controls and stable identity outside. Features own loading and the committed key. Children retain DOM identity and local state.

`Metric` accepts optional opaque committed `changeKey`. Changed keys roll the exact incoming formatted value upward within a clip over 200ms; initial and unavailable values stay static. Its keyboard-scrollable region stays stationary.

`SignedBarList` accepts optional opaque committed `changeKey` to replay the rankings entry recipe: rows enter over 300ms and bars grow over 420ms, with 35ms row stagger and ease timing. Rows also animate on insertion; unchanged keys do not replay. Negative signed bars grow from the right baseline.

Metric, SignedBarList, RankingList and ContentChange share internal finite motion presets. Reduced motion skips entry and cancels active animations immediately; skipped keys are remembered. Keep rolling metrics and animated bars outside ContentChange to avoid layering its fade.

`Select` takes an accessible `label`, typed `options` with `value` and `label`, a committed `value`, and `onselect`. It resolves native values against the supplied options before emitting typed values. The displayed value remains committed until the caller updates it, including during navigation. Native attributes pass through.

`ViewButtons` takes a group `label` and native `ViewButton` children. Each button requires `selected` and exposes `aria-pressed`. Use these for local category changes with the tab appearance; all buttons remain in the native Tab order. Use ViewLinks for navigation. ViewLinks defaults to `wrap={false}` and supports `wrap={true}` for wrapping category tabs without changing its default layout.

Each example is a complete Svelte component placed at `src/Example.svelte`. Load `../lib/ui/styles.css` once in `src/routes/+layout.svelte`. These examples use static presentation data; production features supply real URLs and formatted values.

Actions and focus remain neutral in every entity context. Override `--accent` only for entity meaning, such as funder badges, highlights and charts.

`DeclarationList` renders `ol`, `DeclarationCard` renders `li`, and `ValueRow` renders a nested `li`. `.funding-list` is the UI list recipe for reset and spacing.   </DeclarationCard>

```

## Identity and metric

`IdentityHeader` owns its title, metadata paragraph and grid. Supply inline metadata and a native navigation composition. View-specific controls and metrics belong after identity navigation, inside the active view.     Badge,
    Icon,

    ViewLinks,
    ViewLink,
  } from "./lib/ui";

    >{/snippet}

    <ViewLinks label="Example views">

## Native table columns

`DataTable` supplies the caption, `thead`, `tbody` and neutral cell rules. Use actual `th`/`td` classes in the caller for widths and numeric alignment. [FunderSummary](../../FunderSummary.svelte) is the production example. It owns `.recipient-name` and `.recipient-total`; those classes are not reusable UI APIs.

## Reporting period filters

Use the feature-owned `PeriodSelector` for the same native `Select` on member summaries, funder summaries and rankings. Features own typed period options, URL state and navigation; the select retains the committed value while navigation is pending. Keep the metric left and the select right in the feature-owned Summary grid, stacking at narrow widths.

Pass the committed period to `Metric` and `SignedBarList` as `changeKey` for value and bar entry motion. Put other committed results in `<ContentChange changeKey={period}>` after the controls. Keep rolling metrics and animated bars outside that fade. Keep the existing content and key while navigation is pending; update both together when server data arrives. Use ViewLinks with `wrap={true}` and ViewLink for URL-backed category navigation, or ViewButtons and ViewButton for local category selection. Pair the category group with Select for a secondary choice. Features own a flex toolbar with categories first and the select at the opposite edge. Stack the select below the categories on narrow screens. Keep headings above and results below. Select options retain their feature-owned typed values; features own navigation and pending state.

## Principles

Read the leaf skill in full for any principle you apply. Each entry names when it applies. Each leaf is the **principle-<title>** skill, with the title in kebab case, hyphens kept and other punctuation dropped, unless the entry gives its name.

**Core**

- **Laziness Protocol.** Refactoring, sizing a diff, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias to deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.
- **Foundational Thinking.** Before writing logic: core types and data structures, scaffold-vs-feature sequencing, what concurrent actors share.
- **Redesign from First Principles.** Integrating a new requirement into an existing design. Redesign as if it had been foundational from day one.
- **Attack the Premise.** Two or more fixes that share one premise have failed the same gate. Write the premise down and test it directly before you write another fix that assumes it.
- **Subtract Before You Add.** Sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead weight first, then build on the simpler base.
- **Minimize Reader Load.** Reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. Count layers and hidden state, collapse one-caller wrappers, shrink mutable scope.
- **Outcome-Oriented Execution.** Planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture, don't preserve throwaway compatibility states.

- **Exhaust the Design Space.** A novel interaction or architectural decision with no precedent. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare before committing.

- **Boundary Discipline.** Wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Guards at system boundaries, trust internal types, keep business logic pure.
- **Type System Discipline.** Designing types or a signature in any typed language. Make illegal states unrepresentable, brand primitives, parse external data at boundaries.
- **Make Operations Idempotent.** Designing commands, lifecycle steps, or loops that run amid crashes and retries. Converge to the same end state.
- **Migrate Callers Then Delete Legacy APIs.** Introducing a new internal API while old callers exist. Migrate and delete in one wave.

| DataTable                              | Required text `caption`, `head` snippet and body children. Callers supply native rows, cells, scope and column-specific classes. No numeric alignment or column widths are assumed.                                                  |
| IdentityHeader                         | Required `name`, `kind`, `metadata`; optional `values`, `navigation`, `level` 1/2/3.                                                                                                                                                 |
| ResultRow, DeclarationList             | Native `li` and `ol` wrappers; children and optional accessible `label`. ResultRow callers supply their own anchor and may add a root `class` for a local palette.                                                                   |
| SignedBarList                          | `bars: SignedBar[]`, `baseline`; `variant` default or compact. Values are formatted strings; widths and signs come from features.                                                                                                    |
| BarChart, PieChart                     | Typed `ChartBar[]` geometry and `PieSlice[]` presentation data. Features calculate shares, signs and totals. See [RegistrationTimeline](../../RegistrationTimeline.svelte) and [FunderSummary](../../FunderSummary.svelte).          |
| ViewLinks, ViewLink, Pagination        | Native navigation. ViewLinks `align="start"` (default) or `"end"` aligns each wrapped line. ViewLinks `variant="tabs"` (default) or `"filter"` selects underline tabs or wrapping neutral bordered links. Callers own labels, destinations and `aria-current="page"`; Pagination owns bound availability.                                                                                                                                        |
| Icon, IconIndicator                    | Canonical `IconName`; Icon is decorative. IconIndicator owns focus, pointer and Escape hints.                                                                                                                                        |
| HighlightedText, Spinner, SkeletonRows | Literal text highlights and decorative progress.                                                                                                                                                                                     |

The first DataTable body row has a top divider, including when callers visually hide column headings.

Classes on native-attribute components accept Svelte class arrays and objects. Where a structural component exposes `class`, it adds a root hook. No class replacement API is supported. Use finite variants for existing appearances; caller-authored snippet classes own feature text and arrangements. The recipes show those classes explicitly.

Tokens in [tokens.css](tokens.css) own colors, spacing, type and focus. Override `--accent` on a container for another palette, such as `var(--accent-funder)`. The Exposed wordmark stays white across entity contexts. The landing heading uses member purple for MPs and funder teal for financial interests. Entity indicators, badges, highlights, charts and declared values derive their colors from the local accent; a ResultRow root `class` can select that palette explicitly. Actions use neutral `--action`, `--action-ink`, `--action-border`, `--action-surface` and `--action-hover`; all focus rings use `--focus-color`, independently of entity palettes. Keep action and focus tokens neutral in member and funder containers. `--focus-width` and `--focus-offset` apply at the root or on a container. Native links, buttons and summaries add one pixel to the offset. Do not import internal stylesheets individually.

The [barrel](index.ts) is the public inventory. The gallery covers native disclosure/input behavior, precise metric overflow, repeated association IDs and pointer tooltip lifecycle. Financial parsing and availability decisions belong in feature adapters, never in UI components.

UI-owned snippet classes are `.results-list` (list reset and divider), `.entity-text` (shrinkable content), `.entity-name` (result anchor typography and hover), `.entity-alias` (secondary result text), `.funding-list` (nested list reset and spacing), `.declaration-reference`, `.payment-type`, `.currency-label`, `.empty-entry` (declaration context), `.amount` (exact value typography), and `.entry-count`/`.partial-note` (secondary chart/table text). These work with the single UI stylesheet import. Feature grids and custom table columns stay in callers.

`CategoryWheel` accepts `CategoryWheelOption[]` with caller-owned closed SVG sector `path`, open outer-boundary `rimPath` in the same local coordinates, and label positions, a selected identity, accessible group `label`, optional pixel `size` (default 284), and `onselect`. Native pressed buttons cover the complete sectors. Muted category surfaces, icons, labels and fine inner/radial boundaries stay constant. Selection brightens only the outer rim; focus uses a neutral full-sector outline. A decorative neutral chart glyph occupies the center. Each option has optional `width` and `height`, both defaulting to 142px, for its native button bounds. Callers provide `left` and `top` within the 284px canvas and paths and label positions local to those bounds. Sectors must provide their full bounds so the native hit target covers the path. The gallery updates example uses 284px-wide horizontal halves; ranking quadrants use the default square bounds. Features provide a size that fits the layout.

`RankingList` accepts formatted `RankingRow[]` and an accessible list `label`. Features supply stable keys, destinations, amounts, coverage, signs and bar widths. The list animates row and bar entry and disables animation for reduced motion. Party identities can omit destinations.

`ContentChange` takes a string `changeKey` and `children` snippet. Its persistent root fades new committed content from opacity 0.65 to 1 over 200ms. Initial rendering is static. New changes cancel earlier motion; reduced motion skips animation and cancels active motion when enabled. Keep controls and stable identity outside. Features own loading and the committed key. Children retain DOM identity and local state.

`Metric` accepts optional opaque committed `changeKey`. Changed keys roll the exact incoming formatted value upward within a clip over 200ms; initial and unavailable values stay static. Its keyboard-scrollable region stays stationary.

`SignedBarList` accepts optional opaque committed `changeKey` to replay the rankings entry recipe: rows enter over 300ms and bars grow over 420ms, with 35ms row stagger and ease timing. Rows also animate on insertion; unchanged keys do not replay. Negative signed bars grow from the right baseline.

Metric, SignedBarList, RankingList and ContentChange share internal finite motion presets. Reduced motion skips entry and cancels active animations immediately; skipped keys are remembered. Keep rolling metrics and animated bars outside ContentChange to avoid layering its fade.

`Select` takes an accessible `label`, typed `options` with `value` and `label`, a committed `value`, and `onselect`. It resolves native values against the supplied options before emitting typed values. The displayed value remains committed until the caller updates it, including during navigation. Native attributes pass through.

`ViewButtons` takes a group `label` and native `ViewButton` children. Each button requires `selected` and exposes `aria-pressed`. Use these for local category changes with the tab appearance; all buttons remain in the native Tab order. Use ViewLinks for navigation. ViewLinks defaults to `wrap={false}` and supports `wrap={true}` for wrapping category tabs without changing its default layout.
# Composition recipes

Each example is a complete Svelte component placed at `src/Example.svelte`. Load `../lib/ui/styles.css` once in `src/routes/+layout.svelte`. These examples use static presentation data; production features supply real URLs and formatted values.

Actions and focus remain neutral in every entity context. Override `--accent` only for entity meaning, such as funder badges, highlights and charts.

## Search result

`ResultRow` renders `li`. The caller owns the anchor, metadata and list container. The UI stylesheet owns `.entity-text`, `.entity-name` and `.entity-alias`.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { ResultRow, Badge, IconIndicator } from "./lib/ui";
</script>

<ul class="results-list">
  <ResultRow label="Example Foundation, funder">
    <IconIndicator icon="building" label="Organisation" />
    <div class="entity-text">
      <a
        class="entity-name"
        href="/funders/11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111"
        >Example Foundation</a
      >
      <span class="entity-alias">Also recorded as Example Trust</span>
    </div>
    <Badge>Organisation</Badge>
  </ResultRow>
</ul>
```

## Declaration and value

`DeclarationList` renders `ol`, `DeclarationCard` renders `li`, and `ValueRow` renders a nested `li`. `.funding-list` is the UI list recipe for reset and spacing. The registered snippet is already wrapped in `p`, so supply inline content. The UI stylesheet owns `.payment-type` and `.amount`; the caller supplies the formatted amount.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { DeclarationList, DeclarationCard, ValueRow } from "./lib/ui";
</script>

<DeclarationList label="Example declarations">
  <DeclarationCard>
    {#snippet heading()}<h3>Employment and earnings</h3>{/snippet}
    {#snippet registered()}<time datetime="2026-01-20">20 January 2026</time
      >{/snippet}
    <ul class="funding-list">
      <ValueRow>
        {#snippet source()}
          <a href="/funders/11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111"
            >Example Foundation</a
          >
          <span class="payment-type">Consultancy</span>
        {/snippet}
        {#snippet value()}<span class="amount">£1,234.56</span>{/snippet}
      </ValueRow>
    </ul>
  </DeclarationCard>
</DeclarationList>
```

## Identity and metric

`IdentityHeader` owns its title, metadata paragraph and grid. Supply inline metadata and a native navigation composition. View-specific controls and metrics belong after identity navigation, inside the active view. The optional `values` snippet remains available for standalone identities without view navigation. `Metric` takes exact formatted strings without interpreting money.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import {
    IdentityHeader,
    Badge,
    Icon,
    Metric,
    ViewLinks,
    ViewLink,
  } from "./lib/ui";
</script>

<IdentityHeader name="Jane Example">
  {#snippet kind()}<Badge variant="profile"><Icon name="parliament" />MP</Badge
    >{/snippet}
  {#snippet metadata()}Example Party<span>Example constituency</span>{/snippet}
  {#snippet navigation()}
    <ViewLinks label="Example views">
      <ViewLink href="/members/1" aria-current="page">Summary</ViewLink>
      <ViewLink href="/members/1/history">Declaration history</ViewLink>
    </ViewLinks>
  {/snippet}
</IdentityHeader>

<section aria-label="Summary">
  <Metric variant="expanded" label="Declared amounts" value="£1,234.56" />
</section>
```

## Native table columns

`DataTable` supplies the caption, `thead`, `tbody` and neutral cell rules. Use actual `th`/`td` classes in the caller for widths and numeric alignment. [FunderSummary](../../FunderSummary.svelte) is the production example. It owns `.recipient-name` and `.recipient-total`; those classes are not reusable UI APIs.

## Reporting period filters

Use the feature-owned `PeriodSelector` for the same native `Select` on member summaries, funder summaries and rankings. Features own typed period options, URL state and navigation; the select retains the committed value while navigation is pending. Keep the metric left and the select right in the feature-owned Summary grid, stacking at narrow widths.

Pass the committed period to `Metric` and `SignedBarList` as `changeKey` for value and bar entry motion. Put other committed results in `<ContentChange changeKey={period}>` after the controls. Keep rolling metrics and animated bars outside that fade. Keep the existing content and key while navigation is pending; update both together when server data arrives. Do not key or duplicate the child subtree.

For other native-link filters, use `<ViewLinks variant="filter">` with native `ViewLink` children and `aria-current="page"` on the selected destination. Set `align="end"` for right-aligned filters and keep navigation at full available width so wrapped lines end at the same edge.

## Category toolbar

Use ViewLinks with `wrap={true}` and ViewLink for URL-backed category navigation, or ViewButtons and ViewButton for local category selection. Pair the category group with Select for a secondary choice. Features own a flex toolbar with categories first and the select at the opposite edge. Stack the select below the categories on narrow screens. Keep headings above and results below. Select options retain their feature-owned typed values; features own navigation and pending state.

# TypeScript best practices

On Muse, read the [platform mapping](../poteto-mode/references/muse-tools.md), including its per-skill notes, before following this skill.

Apply the **type-system-discipline** principle skill first.

| Rule | Summary |
|------|---------|
| Discriminated unions | Model variants with a `kind` literal discriminant so impossible states can't be represented. No optional-field bags. |
| Branded types | Brand primitives with `& { readonly __brand: "X" }` so they can't be mixed up. Validate once at the boundary. A brand comes from a verifying type guard (`input is AgentId`), never from `as`. |
| Constructive modeling | Build the shape so the illegal value can't be constructed. `[T, ...T[]]` for non-empty, `[T, T][]` for even length, `start` plus `duration` for a range. Not a runtime guard, not a wish for refinement types. |
| Simplest total type | Keep `T[]` while every operation on it stays total. Strengthen to `NonEmpty<T>` only where the loose type forces `!`, a cast, or a "should never happen" throw. |
| `unknown` over `any` | External data is `unknown`. |
| Schemas before guards | Before hand-writing a property-by-property type guard, use the repository's runtime schema library and infer the type from the schema, such as `z.infer`. |
| No `as` casts | Every `as` is a runtime crash waiting. Cast only after validation. |
| Narrowing hierarchy | Discriminant switch > `in` operator > `typeof`/`instanceof` > user-defined type guard > `as`. |
| Type guards | Must verify the claim. A lying guard is worse than `as` because the bug hides behind a name that says it's safe. Name them `isX` or `hasX`. |
| Exhaustiveness | Inline `const _exhaustive: never = x;` in default arms so the compiler errors when a new variant is added. |
| `satisfies` over `as` | Validates the value without widening literal types. |
| Boundary validation | Parse where data crosses in, into a named domain type. `Record<string, unknown>` (however spelled) stops at that parse. Trust types inside. See the **boundary-discipline** principle skill. |
| Schema-derived types | Reach for `Pick`/`Omit`/`Parameters`/`ReturnType`/`Awaited`/`typeof` before declaring a new interface. |
| Object args | Pass objects, not positional, so argument order is self-documenting. Skip on hot paths (per-frame render, tokenizers, parsers). |
| Real tests | Don't mock what you can run. Prefer the framework's real test primitives with leak/disposable checks, and verify UI in a running build. Mock only what you can't run locally. |
| Structured telemetry | Prefer structured logger diagnostics with enough context to debug from an id. No `console.log` in shipped code. |

Examples: `references/patterns.md`.

# Database migrations

[SQLx CLI 0.9.0](https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/tree/v0.9.0/sqlx-cli) applies
versioned reversible migrations from `db/migrations`. The application exposes
`exposed migrate run` as an explicit migration command. Server startup and data
commands do not apply migrations. Run these commands from the repository root:

```sh
sqlx migrate run --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations
sqlx migrate info --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations
```

To apply migrations with the application binary:

```sh
exposed migrate run
exposed migrate run --source /srv/exposed/migrations
```

The default source is `db/migrations`, relative to the current working directory.
The binary reads migration files at runtime and applies pending up migrations.
It returns `{"source":"db/migrations"}` on stdout after success, or the existing
JSON error envelope on stderr with exit code 1 after failure. The response's
`source` is the supplied path. Use SQLx CLI for adding, inspecting, or reverting
migrations. The wrapper does not read `sqlx.toml`; it fixes the same history table
at `public._sqlx_migrations` and retains SQLx's locking and checksum checks.

Commands read the root `.env`. Set `DATABASE_URL` explicitly to target another
database. The root [`sqlx.toml`](../sqlx.toml) fixes the history table at
`public._sqlx_migrations`, regardless of the connection's search path.
Run only one import or migration against a database at a time.

## Add or revert a migration

Create a versioned pair with SQLx:

```sh
sqlx migrate add --source db/migrations --reversible describe_the_change
```

Write the schema change in the generated `.up.sql` file and its reverse in the
matching `.down.sql` file. Keep applied migrations immutable. Add new versions
for later changes instead of editing the baseline or creating `db/upgrades`
scripts. SQLx runs each direction in a transaction; omit `BEGIN` and `COMMIT`.

To revert the latest applied version:

```sh
sqlx migrate revert --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations
```

Each invocation reverts one version. The current chain creates the normalized
member, declaration, funder, and funding tables, then adds the resolved declaration
loader, then adds the search indexes. Revert these in reverse order. Reverting
the loader drops its aliases, load history, and attribution columns. It also
restores unique funder names, so duplicate names cause the whole revert to fail
without changing the schema. Reverting the baseline removes all domain data,
`pg_trgm`, and the `exposed` schema. Unexpected dependencies fail transactionally
because the down migrations do not use `CASCADE`.

Test both a populated forward upgrade and the complete down/up cycle in an
isolated database before applying a new migration to imported data.

## Transition from the consolidated baseline once

Earlier development versions folded the loader and search changes into
`20260915000000_initial.up.sql`. The migration chain now assigns those changes
their own versions. An existing database with the consolidated baseline already
has the latest schema, but SQLx rejects the changed baseline checksum.
